newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia reiterates Asia outlook, rejects Hanson.
newsitem.headline: Australia reiterates Asia outlook, rejects Hanson.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer reiterated on Monday his country's determination to be part of Asia and rejected what he called the "narrow-minded" views of populist politician Pauline Hanson.

"The vitality of Australia's modern relationship with Indonesia and, indeed, the strength of Australia's other partnerships across the region, should leave us in no doubt about the paramount importance of closer engagement with Asia," Downer told an Indonesia-Australia business meeting in Denpasar on the resort island of Bali.
"There are dissonant voices in our society, most notably Pauline Hanson and the One Nation Party, which do not see Australia's future with Asia.

"I have said repeatedly over the last eight months and I want to repeat again today that those views promote an insular Australia, inward looking, narrow-minded, protectionist and separate from the region," he said in a speech.

Downer was speaking at the 24th Joint Conference of Indonesia-Australia Business Council (IABC) and the Australia-Indonesia Business Council (AIBC), which promotes business co-operation between the two countries.
Downer also said he rejected the idea of turning Australia into a vocal human rights campaigner in Asia.

"...and those who are suddenly arguing that Australia should turn its foreign policy on its head and be the most publicly vocal, aggressive campaigner on human rights in Asia, rather than striving in a more Asian way to achieve results, I say they are not serious about engagement with Asia," he said.
"They hanker for an earlier era. They, too, would confine Australia to a lonely future," he added.

Hanson, a former fish-and-chip shop proprietor from conservative Queensland state, has attracted support from about 10 percent of the country's voters with her criticism of multi-culturalism, Aborginal welfare, economic reform and immigration, especially Asian immigration.

The debate that Hanson has stirred up has divided Australia, and her political rallies have been accompanied by hostile demonstrations against her, although a gathering in northern Queensland last week passed peacefully.
